payload.previous_proof_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x, and let m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m <= x < m + 1. Define f = x - m. Then 0 <= f < 1, and x = m + f. Since frac(x) denotes the fractional part of x, we have frac(x) = x - floor(x) = f. Therefore x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1. This holds for every real x, so the lemma is proved.

result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. Set m = floor(x). By definition of the floor function, m is an integer and m <= x < m + 1. Define f = x - m. Then f >= 0 because x >= m, and f < 1 because x < m + 1. Also, by the definition of fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m = f. Hence x = m + f = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real x.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the defining property of floor to write x = floor(x) + (x - floor(x)), and note that the remainder lies in [0,1).
